title: Witten: Townsend Brown's antigravity bismuth isotope

tellings.quote: he says that he was contracted by right Airfield to work on gravity and he said that there was a guy named townzen who had a weird isotope of bismuth that exhibited anti-gravity properties

plain: In the 1950s, a man named Louis Witten says, Wright Field, a military airfield, hired him to work on gravity, and a man named Thomas Townsend Brown had an unusual form of bismuth, a metal, that seemed to show anti-gravity properties. Michels passes this on from what Witten says, and the story also ties in a company called the Martin Corporation. If true, it would mean the military was quietly chasing anti-gravity research decades ago.
